title: Visual loss: eye examination
stem: Cubicle 27. Mr Kwan, 70, with hypertension and AF, noticed this morning that he keeps bumping into things on his right. Perform an eye examination and explain your management plan. A Snellen chart, pinhole, torch and ophthalmoscope are available.

phases.title: Present and plan
phases.goal: Where is the lesion, and what now?

notes:
Checked against RCOphth guidance, NICE NG128 (stroke and TIA), and standard eye examination.

Examination: acuity with a Snellen chart at 6 m (each eye, with glasses; pinhole to correct refractive error), inspection, pupils (direct, consensual, swinging-light for RAPD), eye movements, visual fields by confrontation (each eye, each quadrant; red target for central fields), fundoscopy (red reflex, disc, vessels, macula). A homonymous hemianopia (same side in both eyes) localises behind the chiasm — optic tract, radiation or occipital cortex — usually a stroke in the posterior cerebral artery territory; acuity and fundi are normal. It needs urgent stroke assessment (CT/CTA; thrombolysis if within the window and disabling), and advice not to drive.

Other patterns: monocular sudden painless loss (CRAO — cherry-red spot; CRVO — 'stormy sunset'; retinal detachment; GCA), bitemporal hemianopia (chiasm — pituitary), painful red eye with a mid-dilated pupil (acute angle-closure glaucoma).

Your notes (2021 past paper: right homonymous hemianopia, normal acuity with pinhole, no RAPD, normal fundi) match this.

Perfect script checked against RCOphth guidance and NICE NG128, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the optician option.

steps.label: Examine the eyes
steps.hint: Acuity (pinhole), inspection, pupils (RAPD), movements, fields, fundoscopy.

Acuity.t: Visual acuity with the Snellen chart at 6 metres, each eye in turn, with his glasses
Acuity.mark: Measures visual acuity in each eye

Acuity.t: Now through a pinhole, to correct any refractive error
Acuity.r: Both improve to 6/6 — refractive error only.
Acuity.mark: Uses a pinhole to correct refractive error

Pupils and movements.t: Pupils: direct and consensual reflexes, then the swinging light test for a relative afferent pupillary defect
Eye movements: follow my finger; tell me if you see double

Fields.t: Visual fields by confrontation, each eye separately, all four quadrants
Fields.r: Both eyes miss the right half of the field: right homonymous hemianopia.

Fundus.t: Fundoscopy: the red reflex, the disc, the vessels and the macula

steps.ask: Thank you. Please present your findings and your plan.
steps.label: Present and plan
steps.hint: Localise: left post-chiasmal (occipital) lesion — stroke pathway.

opts.t: Right homonymous hemianopia with normal acuity, pupils and fundi: a left post-chiasmal lesion, likely a left occipital, PCA infarct, given his AF.
opts.mark: Localises the lesion and suggests the cause

opts.t: Stroke team now: urgent CT and CTA; thrombolysis if within 4.5 hours and disabling; check his anticoagulation.
He mustn't drive; formal visual fields; secondary prevention, with anticoagulation for the AF.

qs.q: Bitemporal hemianopia suggests a lesion at…
wrong: One optic nerve, anterior to the chiasm

qs.q: Cherry-red spot at the macula suggests…
wrong: Central retinal vein occlusion with macular oedema

qs.q: Painful red eye, fixed mid-dilated pupil, halos, vomiting?

qs.a: Shows whether poor acuity is refractive
wrong: Tests the peripheral visual fields, one quadrant at a time

badge.name: Field Marshal
badge.flavor: Same half in both eyes: it's the brain, not the eye.

cards.why: Optic tract, radiation or occipital cortex.

cards.q: Sudden painless monocular loss in a patient over 50 with headache and jaw claudication?
options: A mature cataract in the affected eye
Double vision on lateral gaze with ptosis
A pale disc with sharp margins (optic atrophy)
A cherry-red spot at the macula with a pale retina
Cotton wool spots only, no haemorrhages

script.say: Visual acuity with the Snellen chart at 6 metres, each eye in turn, with his glasses. Now through a pinhole, to correct any refractive error. Pupils: direct and consensual reflexes, then the swinging light test for a relative afferent pupillary defect.
script.do: Right 6/9, left 6/9. Both improve to 6/6 — refractive error only. Equal, reactive, no RAPD.

script.say: Eye movements: follow my finger; tell me if you see double. Visual fields by confrontation, each eye separately, all four quadrants. Fundoscopy: the red reflex, the disc, the vessels and the macula.
script.do: Full, no diplopia or nystagmus. Both eyes miss the right half of the field: right homonymous hemianopia. Normal discs and vessels.
